title: Decision map: choose the layout
question: Same visual identity, three ways to inspect a call. Choose the layout to build. Each uses recorded gates only and keeps actual execution separate.

options.label: 01 · Open map
options.thesis: The whole decision reads as one uninterrupted diagram.
options.viewport: The selected call spans a full-width map; its explanation and evidence controls sit below.
options.risk: Many rules need grouping, and detailed evidence uses space below the map.
options.case: Your chosen concept, unchanged. Motion traces the selected connection once and opens evidence beneath it.

options.label: 02 · Map + evidence
options.thesis: Keep the decision visible while reading a selected gate's evidence.
options.viewport: A broad diagram sits beside a focused right-hand evidence panel. It becomes a bottom sheet on mobile.
options.risk: The diagram has less horizontal space; commands and long rule text need careful wrapping.
options.case: Motion follows your selected node into the evidence panel. Unchanged polling never moves the map.

options.label: 03 · Rule lanes
options.thesis: Give each rule its own readable row without losing the overall decision.
options.viewport: The action and policy result frame stacked rule lanes; each lane shows its outcome and confidence checks.
options.risk: More information up front, so it feels closer to a debugging view than the open map.
options.case: Expanding a rule opens its evidence in place. Other lanes move together rather than fading in separately.
